FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE September 29, 2022 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2022-2023-1 At the September 8, 2022 meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate. SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate PROGRAM CHANGES COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Department of Textile, Fashion Merchandising and Design BS - Textile Marketing: Change to core courses: Proposal: Add BAI 211 to the TM curriculum requirement, so the Program Description will read ".. ACC 201, ACC 202, BAI 211, INE 315,..." Rationale: Not requiring BAI 211 creates a gap in the path for students in the program. The TM curriculum does not currently require BAI 211 (Managerial Decision Support Systems,) one of MKT 367 Marketing Research's prerequisites, while MKT 367 is a required course for TM. So, in general, TM students do not take BAI 211, and without the prerequisite, need permission numbers to get into MKT 367. Requiring BAI 211 fixes this glitch. With that, the number of non-TMD elective credits available changes from "nine" to "six." Add Electives: Add BAI 458 (Seminar in Management Information Systems) as a Business Elective in TM Add MKT 475 (Social Media for Marketing) as a Business elective in TM Rationale: Students are routinely taking these courses within the program and BAI 458 is already cross-listed as TMD 458. Adding them to the list of electives is helpful in clarifying students' pathway through the program. 1

COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES: Writing and Rhetoric Department: BA - Writing and Rhetoric major: Change name of department; add concentrations within major, revise require courses for major: In keeping with University, College, and Harrington strategic plans, our department has committed to major innovation. We have embarked on a research-based initiative to determine how best to meet the needs of students and of the University as a whole. We have interviewed and/or conducted focus groups with students, faculty, and alumni; made a careful study of developments in the field of Writing Studies and in the job market; and benchmarked other institutions. Based on this research, the Department of Writing and Rhetoric is proposing the following: ● to change the name of the department to the “Department of Professional and Public Writing” to connect with student interests and needs and to reflect department strengths and learning outcomes; ● add concentration areas in Technical Writing and Professional and Civic Writing in keeping with Goal 4 of the Academic Strategic Plan; and ● modify required courses for the major, adding courses that specifically forward Strategy 1 in the Agenda for Change and eliminating outdated courses. 2
